title: A Cover for the Protocol
premise: Sable Villalobos, a ghost-hand negotiator whose one public failure still haunts the trade, is assigned to extract Marek Dusek, a defector carrying a cryptographic protocol that three governments would kill to bury. When photos of their supposedly unlisted safe house surface in a real-estate listing, Sable realizes the operation was never secret — it's bait, and Dusek may be the hook. As dawn approaches, Sable must decide whether loyalty to her handler or the truth about her old failure matters more, trading her own cover to get Dusek onto the flight. The book ends with the plane airborne, the protocol leaked publicly as insurance, and Sable walking into a new anonymity she chose for herself.
about_author: Zephyrine Underhill is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent seven years listening to people talk their way out of corners. They write thrillers from a farmhouse with deliberately poor cell reception.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Sable arrives at the safe house to prep Dusek's extraction and finds a realtor's flyer on the doorstep — interior photos of rooms only four people have ever seen. The emotional beat is cold dread: invisibility, her entire professional religion, has been revoked overnight.

chapters.title: Cargo With a Pulse
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. She meets Dusek, brittle and brilliant, who insists he's already dead and the protocol is his life insurance. Sable runs counter-surveillance and finds the listing traces back to a shell company she recognizes from her failed negotiation years ago. Beat: reluctant partnership forming under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Board Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Sable, flashback-weighted. We learn of the Ostrava failure — the hostage she talked into surrendering who died anyway — and how her handler, Ilsa Rehn, buried the report that would have cleared her. Beat: grief weaponized into competence.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Sable/Dusek. A stranger tours the safe house while they hide in the crawlspace; Dusek whispers that the protocol can identify whoever sold them out. Beat: claustrophobic terror curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Rehn's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Sable confronts Ilsa via burner call; Ilsa admits the listing is deliberate — headquarters wants Dusek taken en route, and Sable was chosen because her failure makes her deniable. Beat: betrayal landing like a diagnosis.

chapters.title: Two Exits, One Road
chapters.summary: POV: Dusek. Dusek reveals a second extraction option through a smuggler who owes him, but it means trusting a man who once sold him out. Sable must choose between the sanctioned route (a trap) and the unsanctioned one (a gamble). Beat: decision under duress.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Negotiation set-piece at a river depot; Sable talks the smuggler down from demanding the protocol itself to accepting leverage — she offers him the proof of who betrayed Dusek. Beat: her craft working again, and costing her something real.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The trap springs early — Ilsa's team hits the depot, the smuggler flips, and Sable uses herself as the negotiating chip to buy Dusek the runway to the airstrip. Beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Face-to-face with Ilsa at gunpoint, Sable forces the truth of Ostrava onto an open channel, making her own exoneration worthless but Ilsa's position untenable. Dusek's plane lifts off as Sable surrenders. Beat: triumph shaped like defeat.

chapters.title: A Cover for the Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Dusek, coda. Weeks later, the protocol surfaces publicly, Ilsa is consumed by the fallout, and Sable — released, unlisted, untraceable — receives a postcard with no return address. Beat: quiet resolution; she finally owns her own cover story.
